correctness.rationale: Using exactly the original lattice-slice sum, power sums up to cubic give a factored degree-four Ehrhart polynomial; the polynomial-identity checker independently verifies this algebra. The h* numerator follows by finite differences; its degree-three discriminant factors into a positive polynomial for c>=1, while c=0 has a strictly real-rooted quadratic. The remaining Ehrhart quadratic has discriminant c^2(c^2-12c-12), yielding c=13 as exact first appearance of two positive roots. Coefficient roots give thresholds 10 and 12. No numerical sampling is used as infinite proof.

This reveals sharp, simultaneous positivity-versus-spectral behavior in a canonical smooth family and supplies an infinite structural comparison, not an arbitrary special-value calculation.
